explanation: Operator overloading in C++ allows developers to define custom behaviors for built-in operators (such as +, -, *, etc.) when applied to user-defined types like classes and structs. This feature enables more intuitive and readable code by allowing objects to interact using familiar operators, effectively extending the language's syntax to work seamlessly with complex data types. It is particularly useful in implementing mathematical, container, or resource-managing classes where natural operator semantics improve code clarity and expressiveness.
